subject: Next steps: Nimbus evaluation, model recommendations, and stability controls
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Torres <lena.torres@nimbus.solutions>
Cc: Phil Grant <phil.grant@nimbus.solutions>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + evaluation next steps (post-discovery)

Hi Lena — great conversation this morning. Recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal: validate model fit for Nimbus's internal support triage use case (short text classification + structured extraction for case routing).
- What we’ll send: an evaluation pack with sample prompts, a small benchmark harness, and recommended model variants to try.
- Timeline: I’ll drop the eval artifacts today; would you be able to run the harness against a 1k-sample subset early next week?

Immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm a contact for technical access (token/whitelisted IP) — Phil ok to be the primary?
2) Share any redline constraints (PII handling, retention, audit) we should bake into the eval.

I’m attaching a lightweight eval pack that includes a prompt set and example metrics collector. I’ll follow up with a short internal note to align on recommended model variants and a pin/rollback plan given your concern about regressions.

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nimbus_eval_pack_v1.zip (contains prompt_set_nimbus.md, harness_instructions.md)

From: Lena Torres <lena.torres@nimbus.solutions>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Phil Grant <phil.grant@nimbus.solutions>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + evaluation next steps (post-discovery)

Thanks Rafael — that aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications before you send the full pack: 

- Model stability: last year we saw a delivery regression when the vendor rolled a minor model update; we cannot tolerate production regressions that increase false positives in routing. Can you outline the ability to pin and a rollback SLA?
- Benchmarking: if possible, include a deterministic eval harness (same seeds, same preproc) so we can reproduce numbers here.

Phil will be our technical lead for the evaluation. He’ll be on the setup calls next week.

Lena
Head of Customer Experience
Nimbus Solutions

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Torres <lena.torres@nimbus.solutions>, Phil Grant <phil.grant@nimbus.solutions>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Nimbus eval — model recommendations + stability controls

Team — quick internal plan to respond to Lena's stability question and to recommend model variants for the eval. Posting the items I intend to send to the customer unless there are objections.

Summary for customer-facing note: 
- Recommended variants: redwood-4k-standard, redwood-4k-quantized-INT8, and redwood-llm-slim-2 (for latency-sensitive routing).
- Benchmarks: include our reproducible harness (seeded), a 1k sample pass with per-class precision/recall, and token-level latency distributions. Link to sample results: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/DEAL-7821 (we should upload the CSV).
- Pinning & rollback plan:
  * We can pin a model version for the customer environment for the trial (pin is immediate; automatic fallback to prior pinned version if automated checks fail).
  * Suggested guardrail: snapshot baseline metrics (golden set). If a new version shows >5% absolute degradation on routing F1 on the golden set, auto-rollback triggers.
  * SLA ask: commit to a 4-hr rollback window for Dedicated and a same-business-day advisory for Hosted (we'll need to confirm with product/legal).

Files to attach to the customer reply: prompt_set_nimbus.md, benchmark_results_summary.csv (sample), and the eval harness instructions. Draft contract addendum for rollback/SLA (Laura to review).

Key asks to internal team:
- Prioym: can you validate the recommended quantized flavor and add notes on expected latency/throughput and any KV-cache effects?
- Aditya: can you confirm the feasibility of auto-rollback based on the metric threshold and estimate engineering lead time for a Hosted rollback SLA?
- Laura: please draft a brief addendum covering rollback window and credits for stability regressions (we’ll keep it conservative for the early trial).

I’ll send the customer-facing note once I have your quick take.

—Rafael

From: Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Torres <lena.torres@nimbus.solutions>, Phil Grant <phil.grant@nimbus.solutions>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Nimbus eval — model recommendations + stability controls

Rafael — quick technical notes for the thread reply: 

- Quantized variant: redwood-4k-quant-INT8 is safe for inference here; expect ~25% lower token cost and ~10–15% latency delta versus the standard float variant. For classification-heavy workloads latency improves for batched scoring but single-request p99 may increase ~5–10ms depending on seq length.
- Pinning mechanics: we maintain model-version tags. Pin = send model_version_id to runtime routing config. We can snapshot a pinned model and maintain a read-only copy for quick fallback. For Hosted customers we can enable an immediate rollback route (route flags) that swaps traffic back to the snapshot.
- Auto-rollback criteria: agree with Rafael's 5% absolute F1 drop on golden set; recommend adding a secondary check for high-severity false-positive increase (>3 percentage points) to prevent churn in routing.
- Engineering lift: Hosted auto-rollback using our existing route-flag mechanism is doable, estimate 2–3 business days for customer-specific gating and audit hooks; Dedicated/Private has faster ops path (within same-day).

I attached a short CSV with sample benchmark expectations and a small prompt_set_nimbus.md excerpt.

—Prioym
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark_results_summary.csv, prompt_set_nimbus.md

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Torres <lena.torres@nimbus.solutions>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Phil Grant <phil.grant@nimbus.solutions>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Nimbus evaluation agreement & rollback language (draft)

Hi Lena — thanks for flagging the stability concern. I’ve drafted a short addendum that we can include with the trial statement of work. Highlights: 

- Rollback window: Redwood will commit to a 4-hour rollback for Dedicated customers; for the Hosted trial we propose a same-business-day rollback with a maximum of 8 business-hours response for activation of rollback.
- Credits: If a regression (as defined by agreed thresholds) causes measurable routing loss in production, we will credit the customer for impacted minutes/hours (capped per the trial).
- Pinning: We will pin the evaluation to a model_version_id on Day 0; any model change requires explicit opt-in unless auto-rollback is triggered.

I’m attaching a draft doc with wording that your procurement team can review: contract_sla_addendum_draft.docx. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through language. Rafael — feel free to send the consolidated customer reply when ready.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: contract_sla_addendum_draft.docx
